title.narrative: Strengthening Health Emergency Response in six priority districts affected by Drought, Cholera and Tropical Cyclone Chido in Malawi

description.narrative: The World Health Organization (WHO) is proposing a project titled “Strengthening Health Emergency Response in six priority districts affected by Drought and Tropical Cyclone Chido in Malawi”. The proposed project seeks to mitigate the dual impacts of drought due to El Nino and Tropical Cyclone Chido in the context of ongoing cholera outbreaks in the country. Tropical Cyclone Chido has exacerbated public health vulnerabilities by damaging critical infrastructure including health facilities and WASH infrastructure, displacing communities, and increasing the risk of waterborne diseases. Malawi has in the recent past responded to various natural disasters including Tropical Storm Ana, Tropical Cyclones Gombe and Freddy, and floods. The impacts of such disasters have increased risks to infectious disease outbreaks such as cholera. The recent protracted cholera outbreak in Malawi resulted in 59,376 cases and more than 1,772 deaths (CFR = 3%). The country’s vulnerability to such public health emergencies is still high and contributes to significant loss of life and health. They also impose great strains on an already fragile health system that has not had an opportunity to recover from previous and ongoing shocks. Furthermore, these challenges have also contributed to food insecurity situation among the majority of people resident in the affected districts. In March 2024, a State of Disaster was declared by the President in 23 out of Malawi’s 29 districts due to El Niño conditions. Between May and September 2024, approximately 4.2 million people faced acute food insecurity (Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC Phase 3 or above - ‘crisis’) with an additional 6.7 million people classified as IPC level 2 (‘stressed’). This situation is expected to deteriorate during the October 2024 - March 2025 lean season with the Malawi Vulnerability Assessment Committee (MVAC) Assessment predicting that 5.7 million people (28 per cent of the population) will be in IPC Phase 3 or above. A known consequence of drought and its associated risk factors is infectious disease outbreaks including Cholera, which are worsened by malnutrition, poor access to water, sanitation, and hygiene. On September 9th, 2024, a new outbreak was declared in Chitipa district, that has since spread to other districts. Considering inherent WASH vulnerabilities and the start of the rainy season, the situation is predicted to get worse. The project will support the delivery of time-critical, life-saving health services to people in six high-priority drought- and cyclone affected districts of Mangochi, Machinga, Balaka, Zomba, Mulanje and Thyolo. This project will provide immediate life-saving interventions, including the establishment of temporary health service points, health facility repairs, provision of essential medicines and medical supplies, deployment of rapid response teams to respond to related disease outbreaks, including cholera. The project will also enable strengthening of early warning systems, community engagement, as well as IPC/WASH to reduce the spread of cholera and thereby contain the outbreaks. Consequently, WHO will reach 15,000 people in target locations with different health interventions. The target beneficiaries are people affected by Cyclone Chido in Mangochi (2850), Machinga (3300), Balaka (1650), Zomba (1200), Mulanje (3450) and Thyolo (2550) districts, which have also reported cholera outbreaks.
